issues.description: Cycle detection in push() may misidentify already-sorted nodes as cycles
issues.detail: Previously, 'working' marked nodes currently on the stack and 'sorted' marked completed ones, so push() could distinguish them. Now 'walking' is used both for nodes being processed and remains set until after yield. If a yielded-but-not-yet-sorted node is encountered via another root, push() will run LastIndexFunc and treat it as a cycle, even though it's already emitted.

issues.description: State transition from walking to sorted happens only inside the yield branch
issues.detail: The new code sets s.state[k] = sorted only when state != sorted. If a node is revisited (state already sorted from another path) the assignment is skipped, which is fine, but the asymmetry means a node remains 'walking' until its second visit pops it. Any push() call between first and second visit may incorrectly trigger cycle handling rather than a no-op.
The comment now reads 'visisted' (should be 'visited') and 'if its the first' (should be "if it's the first"). Minor but worth fixing since this PR specifically touches that comment block.

issues.description: No regression test accompanies the state-reuse fix
issues.detail: The PR title is 'Fix state reuse', implying a previously broken scenario when the Sorter is reused across calls (non-zero stack residue, stale state). No test is added to lock in the fix, so a future refactor could silently regress. A test calling Sort twice on the same Sorter with overlapping/disjoint graphs would suffice.

issues.description: Defer-based cleanup runs even on early yield return, which is correct but worth verifying for panics
issues.detail: The new defer clears state, stack, and resets iterating. If yield panics, cleanup still runs - good. But clear(s.stack) on a slice of Node pointers/interfaces is necessary to drop references; confirm Node type holds references worth clearing for GC. For value types this is wasted work; for reference types it's the point.

review.summary: The PR consolidates the 'working' and 'walking' states and moves cleanup into a defer, which simplifies state management and ensures reuse safety. The main concern is the semantic collapse of 'working' and 'walking': push()'s cycle-detection branch now fires for any node in the 'walking' state, but the transition to 'sorted' is delayed until after yield, leaving a window where push() behavior may differ subtly from before. Comment typos were introduced ('visisted', 'if its'), and no test is added to lock in the reuse fix. Overall the change looks correct for the stated bug but would benefit from a regression test and a closer look at the merged-state semantics.
